action: Activate chest pain protocol. ECG within 10 minutes. Call emergency services if out of hospital.
Activate stroke protocol. Note time of onset. CT head urgently. Consider thrombolysis window (4.5h).
Urgent CT head. If negative and high clinical suspicion, LP at 12 hours. Neurosurgical referral.
Immediate IV antibiotics (ceftriaxone). Do not delay for LP. Blood cultures. Dexamethasone.
Sepsis Six within 1 hour: blood cultures, IV antibiotics, IV fluids, measure lactate, urine output, oxygen.
IM adrenaline 0.5mg (adult) immediately. High-flow oxygen. IV fluid bolus. Call for help.
Do NOT delay for imaging. Needle decompression 2nd ICS MCL immediately. Then chest drain.
Assess with Wells score. CTPA urgently. Anticoagulate immediately if high probability. Thrombolysis if massive PE.
Urgent CT aortogram. Control BP (target SBP <120). IV labetalol. Immediate surgical referral if type A.
Urgent echocardiogram. Emergency pericardiocentesis. IV fluid bolus. Do NOT give diuretics.
Check ketones and VBG. Start IV fluids and fixed-rate insulin infusion. Potassium replacement. Monitor hourly.
Check capillary glucose immediately. If <4mmol/L: oral glucose if conscious, IV dextrose/IM glucagon if unconscious.
Urgent vascular surgery referral. Heparin bolus. CT angiogram. Surgery within 6 hours to salvage limb.
Urgent MRI whole spine. Do NOT delay. Emergency surgical decompression if confirmed.
IV dexamethasone 16mg immediately. Urgent MRI whole spine. Neurosurgical/oncology referral.
Urgent serum beta-hCG and transvaginal US. IV access and group & save. Surgical referral if ruptured.
Resuscitate with IV fluids. Group and cross-match. IV PPI. Urgent endoscopy within 24h. Terlipressin if variceal.
Emergency surgical exploration. IV broad-spectrum antibiotics (meropenem + clindamycin). Do NOT delay for imaging.
IV lorazepam (or buccal/rectal if no access). Airway protection. If refractory: IV phenytoin/levetiracetam. Intubation if needed.
Primary PCI within 120 minutes (door-to-balloon). If PCI unavailable, thrombolysis within 12h. DAPT + anticoagulation.
Do NOT delay for imaging if clinical suspicion is high. Urgent surgical exploration within 6 hours.
Remove all casts and dressings. Measure compartment pressures. Emergency fasciotomy if confirmed.
Continuous nebulised salbutamol. IV magnesium sulphate 2g. IV aminophylline if no response. Intubation if deteriorating.
Do NOT examine throat. Call ENT and anaesthetics immediately. Prepare for intubation. IV antibiotics.
IV N-acetylcysteine if paracetamol. ITU referral. Apply King's College criteria. Contact liver transplant centre.
IV hydrocortisone 100mg immediately. IV normal saline bolus. IV dextrose if hypoglycaemic. Do NOT delay for cortisol result.
IV propranolol. IV hydrocortisone. Propylthiouracil loading dose. Lugol iodine (1h after PTU). ICU admission.
IV piperacillin-tazobactam within 1 hour. Blood cultures from all lines. Do NOT delay antibiotics for results.
Serial FVC monitoring every 4h. Intubate if FVC <20ml/kg or declining rapidly. IVIg or plasma exchange.
Lie bleeding side down. High-flow oxygen. Tranexamic acid. Urgent bronchoscopy or bronchial artery embolisation.
Pilocarpine drops. Timolol drops. IV acetazolamide. Urgent ophthalmology for laser iridotomy.
IV labetalol for BP. IV MgSO4 for seizure prophylaxis. Plan delivery. Senior obstetric review.
Emergency delivery (C-section if fetal distress). IV fluids and blood products. Correct coagulopathy.
Serial FVC monitoring. Intubate if FVC <20ml/kg. IVIg or plasma exchange. Avoid aminoglycosides.
IV Pabrinex immediately. Give thiamine BEFORE any glucose. Do NOT delay for investigation.

anyOfFeatures: pain out of proportion to examination
action: Urgent CT mesenteric angiogram. IV fluids. Anticoagulation. Emergency surgical/IR revascularisation.
Erect CXR or CT abdomen. IV antibiotics. IV fluids. Urgent surgical review.
Terlipressin + IV antibiotics immediately. Blood products. Urgent endoscopy for band ligation. TIPS if refractory.
Remove from source. 100% oxygen via non-rebreather. Check COHb level. Hyperbaric oxygen if severe.
Urgent MRI whole spine with contrast. Blood cultures. Urgent surgical drainage. IV antibiotics.
Treat underlying cause aggressively. Cryoprecipitate if fibrinogen <1.5. Platelets if <30 and bleeding. FFP if PT prolonged.
Aggressive IV fluid resuscitation (target UO 200-300ml/h). Monitor K+ and renal function. Consider RRT.
Treat hyperkalaemia urgently. Stop nephrotoxins. Assess fluid status. Renal ultrasound. Consider RRT if refractory.
IV calcium gluconate 10ml 10% immediately. Insulin-dextrose. Salbutamol nebuliser. Cardiac monitoring. Consider dialysis.
Hypertonic saline 100ml 3% NaCl over 10 min (may repeat x2). Correct by <=10mmol/24h. ITU monitoring.
Rapid evaporative cooling. Ice packs to axillae/groin. IV cold fluids. Benzodiazepines for shivering. ICU.
Stop suspected drug immediately. Transfer to burns unit. Wound care. Consider IVIg or cyclosporin. Ophthalmology review.
IV antibiotics. IV fluids. Urgent ERCP for biliary drainage within 24h. Blood cultures.
Exclude organic causes: check glucose, U&E, TFTs, calcium, urine drug screen, CT head. Do NOT assume psychiatric until medical causes excluded.
IV/IM naloxone 400mcg, titrate to respiratory rate. Maintain airway. Prolonged observation (re-sedation risk with long-acting opioids).
Bimanual compression. Oxytocin 40IU infusion. Ergometrine. Carboprost. Examine for trauma. Theatre if medical management fails.
Urgent ophthalmology referral. Same-day assessment if macula-on (better prognosis). Surgical repair.
High-dose prednisolone 60mg immediately (+ IV methylprednisolone if visual loss). Do NOT wait for biopsy. Urgent ophthalmology.
